entry.title: JBossWS 7.4.1.Final is released!
entry.content:
In this release we upgraded Apache CXF to 4.1.8, which includes a security improvement that blocks decoupled WS-Addressing destinations by default as a hardening measure against SSRF attacks. JBossWS-CXF enables decoupled WS-Addressing destinations by default to preserve backward compatibility, while allowing users to opt out and leverage the new Apache CXF security behaviour via the org.jboss.ws.cxf.decoupledEndpointEnabled property.

This release also marks the point where the 7.4.x maintenance branch will be created in the jbossws-cxf repository, as development moves on to the next major release. See the GitHub discussion for more details.

Please try out this release, and let us know if you have any issues or questions.

Release notes - JBoss Web Services - jbossws-cxf-7.4.1.Final

Full release report: JBWS 7.4.1.Final

Component Upgrade

  • JBWS-4521 - Upgrade Apache CXF from 4.1.6 to 4.1.8

  • JBWS-4522 - Upgrade com.google.cloud.tools:jib-maven-plugin from 3.4.3 to 3.5.2

  • JBWS-4523 - Upgrade org.apache.logging.log4j:log4j-1.2-api from 2.23.1 to 2.26.1

  • JBWS-4524 - Upgrade org.apache.neethi:neethi from 3.2.2 to 3.2.3

Task

  • JBWS-4525 - (jbossws-cxf) - Update the project README to reflect the current release procedure
entry.summary: In this release we upgraded Apache CXF to 4.1.8, which includes a security improvement that blocks decoupled WS-Addressing destinations by default as a hardening measure against SSRF attacks. JBossWS-CXF enables decoupled WS-Addressing destinations by default to preserve backward compatibility, while allowing users to opt out and leverage the new Apache CXF security behaviour via the org.jboss.ws.cxf.decoupledEndpointEnabled property.

entry.title: JBossWS 7.4.0.Final is released!
entry.content:
In this release we upgraded Apache CXF to 4.1.6, aligned Jakarta and JBoss dependencies to WildFly, and moved to jboss-jakarta-xml-ws-api 4.0 spec.

Please try out this release, and let us know if you have any issues or questions.

Release notes - JBoss Web Services - jbossws-cxf-7.4.0.Final

Bug

  • JBWS-4488 - jbossws-cxf - “JBWS024029: Cannot obtain destination for …” is thrown when trying to consume a web service having NLS characters in URL path

    • JBossWS-CXF can automatically handle URL-encoded paths containing National Language Symbols (NLS) or other non-ASCII characters.
      The stack can automatically try to decode incoming request paths to match the registered endpoints.

      This behavior is disabled by default and can be controlled globally via the following system properties:

      • org.jboss.ws.cxf.decodeUrlPath - controls the default behavior across all deployments. The default value is false.
      • org.jboss.ws.cxf.urlCharset - controls the charset that will be used to decode the URL path. The default value is UTF-8.

      Such properties can be overridden per-deployment, that is, via the jboss-webservices.xml
      descriptor, which take precedence over the system properties.

      The org.jboss.ws.cxf.urlCharset system property should be aligned with Undertow’s URL\_CHARSET configuration option.

Component Upgrade

  • JBWS-4493 - Move to jboss-jakarta-xml-ws-api_4.0_spec from jboss-jakarta-xml-ws-api_3.0_spec

  • JBWS-4503 - Align jakarta.* and jboss.* dependencies version to WildFly

  • JBWS-4512 - (jbossws-cxf) - Align wildfly* dependencies version to WildFly for jbossws-cxf-7.4.0 consolidation

  • JBWS-4515 - (jbossws-cxf) - Update JBossWS components to the latest released version for jbossws-cxf-7.4.0.Final consolidation

  • JBWS-4518 - (jbossws-cxf) - Upgrade Apache CXF version from 4.1.5 to 4.1.6

Task

  • JBWS-4487 - Upgrade Apache CXF dependencies to 4.1.5

    • Apache CXF was upgraded to 4.1.5, as the 4.0.x stream is no longer maintained, and the 4.2.0 version does not support EE 10.
entry.summary: In this release we upgraded Apache CXF to 4.1.6, aligned Jakarta and JBoss dependencies to WildFly, and moved to jboss-jakarta-xml-ws-api 4.0 spec.

entry.title: JBossWS 7.3.8.Final is released!
entry.content:
In this bugfix release we added a functionality that lets JBossWS CXF accept encoded URL paths, e.g. those including NLS (National Language Symbols) characters in Web Services names.

Please try out this release, and let us know if you have any issues or questions.

Release notes - JBoss Web Services - jbossws-cxf-7.3.8.Final

Bug

  • JBWS-4467 - Tests are searched for in modules/testsuite after maven-surefire-plugin upgrade

  • JBWS-4488 - jbossws-cxf - “JBWS024029: Cannot obtain destination for …” is thrown when trying to consume a web service having NLS characters in URL path

    • JBossWS-CXF can automatically handle URL-encoded paths containing National Language Symbols (NLS) or other non-ASCII characters.
      The stack can automatically try to decode incoming request paths to match the registered endpoints.

      This behavior is disabled by default and can be controlled globally via the following system properties:

      • org.jboss.ws.cxf.decodeUrlPath - controls the default behavior across all deployments. The default value is false.
      • org.jboss.ws.cxf.urlCharset - controls the charset that will be used to decode the URL path. The default value is UTF-8.

      Such properties can be overridden per-deployment, that is, via the jboss-webservices.xml
      descriptor, which take precedence over the system properties.

      The org.jboss.ws.cxf.urlCharset system property should be aligned with Undertow’s URL\_CHARSET configuration option.

Task

  • JBWS-4465 - JBossWS CXF “feature-pack” module does not build against WildFly 39.0.0.Beta1

  • JBWS-4471 - jbossws-cxf - Update to jbossws-parent 2.1.1.Final
entry.summary: In this bugfix release we added a functionality that lets JBossWS CXF accept encoded URL paths, e.g. those including NLS (National Language Symbols) characters in Web Services names.

entry.title: JBossWS 7.3.7.Final is released!
entry.content:
JBossWS-CXF 7.3.7.Final has been released. In this bugfix release we added JDK25 support, fixed expired certificates issue and changed bus default configuration to avoid accumulated cleanup threads leak. For complete issue list, please check the Release Notes.

Please try out this release, and let us know if you have any issues or questions.
